problem:
A quality assurance specialist inspects sealed containers for damaged items. The number of damaged items in each container was recorded and summarized below. If $X$ is the number of damaged items in a container, what is the expected value of $X?$ Do not round the answer.

| Number of Containers | $10$ | $8$ | $6$ | $4$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Damaged Items | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |

$\text{E}[X]=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

We're given the frequencies of the damaged items, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of containers is $10+8+6+4+2=30,$ so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0)=f(0) & =\frac{10}{30} \\ P(X=1)=f(1) & =\frac{8}{30} \\ P(X=2)=f(2) & =\frac{6}{30} \\ P(X=3)=f(3) & =\frac{4}{30} \\ P(X=4)=f(4) & =\frac{2}{30}\end{aligned}
$$

We organize these results in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{10}{30}$ | $\frac{8}{30}$ | $\frac{6}{30}$ | $\frac{4}{30}$ | $\frac{2}{30}$ |

Now, summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =0(\frac{10}{30})+1(\frac{8}{30})+2(\frac{6}{30})+3(\frac{4}{30})+4(\frac{2}{30}) \\  & =\frac{8}{30}+\frac{12}{30}+\frac{12}{30}+\frac{8}{30} \\  & =\frac{40}{30} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
